title: The fast ones leave
hook: A wet arm feels cold. What changes for the molecules that stay behind?

knows: that sweat or a wet arm feels cool
that molecules in a liquid move at different speeds
doesNotKnow: that evaporation cools because the fastest molecules leave and take their energy with them

misconception: Evaporation cools because the liquid 'gives off cold' or because of airflow alone.
objective: The learner can explain that only the most energetic molecules escape a liquid's surface, so the average speed and energy of the rest (its temperature) drop.

claims.text: Molecules in a liquid at one temperature move at a spread of speeds, a few much faster than average.
claims.source: Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution of molecular speeds, valid for translational motion in the classical limit, including in liquids (Atkins, Physical Chemistry, kinetic model of gases; classical equipartition).

claims.text: Stage: 60 water-molecule speeds drawn from the Maxwell–Boltzmann spread at 25 °C, average about 583 m/s (theory 592 m/s).
claims.source: mulberry32 seed 1, untuned; each axis normal with σ = √(kT/m) = 371 m/s, m = 18.015 u. Theoretical mean √(8kT/πm) = 592 m/s. Node script.

claims.text: Removing molecules faster than the average lowers the average of those left.
claims.source: Removing values above the mean lowers the mean (e.g. 1,2,3,4,5 → drop 5 → mean 2.5).

claims.text: Temperature is the average energy of the molecules' motion.
claims.source: Kinetic interpretation of temperature: mean translational KE = (3/2)kT (Atkins, Physical Chemistry). The stage's thermometer shows mean v² as a share of the start.

claims.text: Only molecules with enough energy break free of the surface, so evaporation takes away the high-energy tail; that is how sweat cools you.
claims.source: Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles, 'vapour pressure'; evaporative cooling by sweat (Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, body temperature regulation).

claims.text: Losing 1% of water's mass as vapour cools the rest by about 6 °C.
claims.source: Latent heat of vaporisation of water at 25 °C about 2.44 MJ/kg (CRC Handbook). 0.01 × 2440 kJ / (0.99 kg × 4.18 kJ/(kg K)) = 5.9 K, assuming no heat flows in.

claims.text: With only 60 molecules, each escape moves the average a lot; real water loses a far smaller share.
claims.source: Illustrative sample size; disclosed in the reveal.

claims.text: Stage: only the pink molecules, faster than 750 m/s, can escape; grey columns are too slow to escape. The thermometer's number is the average kinetic energy of the molecules left, as a percentage of the start.
claims.source: Toy rule in Demo.tsx (FAST_BIN = first 150 m/s column wholly above the starting rms speed, 630 m/s, so 750 m/s; energy = meanSq / MS0). Real escape needs energy well above average to overcome the surface attraction, so a high threshold is the honest direction; the exact 750 m/s cut is a toy choice. With seed 1 there are 10 such molecules (809-1198 m/s). | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): new sentence. Slow columns are no longer buttons (r5 blocking finding: slow escapes raised the average). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own re-run seed 1: rms0 629.7 m/s -> FAST_BIN ceil(4.2) = 5 = 750 m/s; 10 molecules >= 750 (809-1198); only bins >= FAST_BIN render as Controls; energy = meanSq / MS0. 750 m/s cut is a disclosed toy choice.

claims.text: When you had let N fast molecules escape, the average speed of the rest had gone from about 583 m/s to X m/s, and the thermometer had fallen to Y% of its start. Each tap lowered both.
claims.source: Values computed in the reveal from the learner's own lowest state. 'Each tap lowered both': every escapable molecule (>= 750 m/s) is above the current mean and rms speed, which only fall, so removing it lowers both mean speed and mean square speed. Builder's node re-run of seed 1, fastest-first: 573/96%, 563/91%, 553/87% ... 504/70% after all 10; one per column (881, 1036, 1198): 559 m/s, 91%. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): new sentence. Replaces the old 'When N molecules had escaped' sentence, which counted slow escapes. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own re-run: mean0 583.4 (583); fastest-first 573/96% ... 504/70%; one per column (881, 1036, 1198) 559/91%. 2,000 random escape orders: every escape lowered both mean speed and mean square speed.

recall.question: A lid keeps the fastest molecules from escaping a cup of tea. Compared with an open cup, the tea cools…
recall.why: Evaporation cools by removing the fastest molecules; blocking their escape removes that cooling.
